name: Ruta Orwell – Monte Irazo & Las Tres Huegas (Sierra de Alcubierre)
story: From late 1936 the Aragon front ran across the bare Sierra de Alcubierre. Anarchist and POUM militia columns faced Nationalist positions such as San Simón, and the front hardly moved for more than a year. The British writer George Orwell served here with the POUM militia, first on Monte Pucero and then on the crest of Monte Irazo until 16 February 1937. He described the cold, the lice and the stalemate in Homage to Catalonia (1938). The Republicans held these positions until the Nationalist Aragon offensive broke the front in March 1938. A monument to the Nationalist side from the 1940s stands on San Simón (699 m).
see: Excavated and rebuilt Republican trenches, rifle pits, an observation post, shelters and a bivouac line with barbed wire on Monte Irazo. Las Tres Huegas has a rebuilt camp with a command post, kitchens, cisterns and a cave shelter. Panels explain the sites.
plan: Monte Irazo is reached by a 1.5 km dirt track from the A-129 at km 34.6 (Alcubierre direction) between Leciñena and Alcubierre. Las Tres Huegas is at about km 33.5. The sites are open-air and free. Bring water and sturdy shoes.
